title: release/ci: generate SBOM for Runtime LTS artifacts
author: Sahana Iyer
description: Motivation: Enterprise Dedicated/Private customers are asking for auditable artifacts for the Runtime LTS line (SBOM + provenance), and several security/compliance reviews are explicitly blocking on “an SBOM for the runtime image and installer payload” (see SUP-18506). This PR adds SBOM generation as part of the LTS release CI pipeline for runtime artifacts (container images + tarball bundles), producing CycloneDX JSON and SPDX JSON outputs that are attached to the release staging bucket and retained with the release manifest. Scope: LTS release branches only (runtime-*-lts), with a safe fallback (“stub mode”) when running in environments without the SBOM tooling available (e.g., restricted runners). Implementation: 1) Introduces a new `tools/sbom/` helper that shells out to Syft when available and normalizes metadata (component name, version, git sha, build timestamp, builder image). 2) Adds a `release/sbom` step to the release-branch GitHub Actions workflow to generate `runtime-<version>-sbom.cdx.json` and `runtime-<version>-sbom.spdx.json` for: (a) the published runtime OCI image digest and (b) the runtime tarball bundle used by Private installer flows. 3) Adds a lightweight validation step that ensures the SBOM contains a top-level component matching the runtime version/tag and includes the base image digest for OCI. 4) Adds “stub support” controlled via `SBOM_MODE=stub` which emits a minimal CycloneDX document with the runtime build metadata (name/version/digest/sha) and a clear `notes` field indicating that full dependency enumeration was not performed. Stub output is rejected for GA LTS releases but allowed for PR CI and local testing to avoid blocking dev flows. 5) Updates release manifest format to include SBOM artifact names + sha256 checksums (pairs with the checksums/provenance work in the LTS artifact pipeline). Notes/constraints: - We intentionally do not attempt to SBOM the host GPU drivers or CUDA runtime on the underlying nodes; SBOM targets only the shipped artifacts. - The tarball SBOM is generated from the extracted filesystem snapshot to avoid “missing files” issues that Syft can hit when scanning compressed layers directly. - For OCI images we scan by digest (not tag) to ensure the SBOM is tied to immutable content. Testing: - Added unit tests for SBOM metadata normalization and for stub-mode output. - Ran workflow on a release-branch dry-run; artifacts are uploaded to the staging bucket and referenced in the generated release manifest. Rollout: - Enabled on `runtime-1.18-lts` immediately. - For mainline releases we keep this disabled for now; once LTS is stable we can consider promoting the job to non-LTS release workflows. Follow-ups: - Document customer-facing SBOM verification steps alongside artifact checksum verification (tracked in ENG-4832). - Evaluate signing SBOMs (in addition to checksums) once signing key policy lands for release branches.
commits: release(ci): add sbom generation step for LTS workflows
tools(sbom): normalize syft output + add stub mode
release(manifest): include sbom artifact names and sha256 entries
tests(sbom): add coverage for metadata + stub output
docs(internal): note sbom gating rules for GA vs PR builds
notable_ci_events: 2025-02-25: sbom-generate failed on first run due to missing `syft` binary on one runner pool; fixed by pinning the tool install step + caching and reran successfully.
2025-02-26: release-branch-ci failed once due to permissions on staging bucket in forked workflow context; adjusted to only upload from trusted contexts and re-ran.
review_conversation: Connor O'Brien: Can we make sure SBOM is generated by image digest, not tag? Tag retargeting would break auditability. Also, what’s our stance on stub mode for actual patch releases? Sahana Iyer: Updated to resolve digest from the published manifest and scan by digest only. Stub mode is now allowed for PR CI/local only; `release_publish=true` requires full mode and fails fast otherwise.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please ensure the SBOM output contains enough metadata to be mapped back to a specific git commit and build invocation. Also, add language that drivers/host deps are out of scope so security reviewers don’t assume coverage. Sahana Iyer: Added `git_sha`, `builder_image`, and `build_timestamp` fields in SBOM `metadata.properties`, and added explicit scope notes in `tools/sbom/README.md` + release manifest README.

Devon Price: Workflow change looks good, but we should avoid making Syft a hard dependency for developers running unit tests. Can the SBOM tooling be isolated to release steps? Sahana Iyer: Yes—Python unit tests do not require Syft. Only the release job installs Syft; the library supports stub mode and tests use fixtures.

Vivek Kulkarni: For Private, do we have a stable path for customers to retrieve the SBOM with the installer bundle? Sahana Iyer: Release manifest now includes SBOM filenames + checksums, and the publish script uploads SBOMs next to the tarball bundle under the same versioned prefix. We’ll reference this in Private upgrade docs in a follow-up.
merge_summary: Merged into runtime-1.18-lts; LTS release CI now emits SBOM artifacts (CycloneDX + SPDX) for runtime OCI image and tarball bundle, updates release manifest to include SBOM checksums, and enforces full SBOM mode for publish builds.
release_notes: LTS release artifacts now include SBOMs (CycloneDX JSON + SPDX JSON) for runtime container images and tarball bundles.
Release manifest includes SBOM filenames and sha256 checksums for easier audit and retrieval.
